_comment: Why each shipped rule and file changed, read by install.py and never installed. Each list holds the versions the bundle has published, oldest first, as the sha256 of the rule body (rules) or of the file (files) with a one-line note saying why it differs from the version before it; only the first entry may have an empty note. A {"removed": true} entry ends a rule or file the bundle no longer ships. Notes are read by strangers: no task numbers, no commit hashes.

executor-briefs-home.note: No longer lists "pinned expectations". That rule was removed from `writing-executor-briefs.md` because it rested on a single incident, and the routing rule says one case does not make a rule.

lesson-routing.note: Adds one exception: a single case the user rules too costly to wait on goes into its home now, untagged, with the reason recorded in the ledger's origin log. The sentence explaining why "provisional" tags fail is gone; probes showed routing behaves the same without it.

search-silence.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. A check for lost meaning found every instruction kept.

end-of-turn-text.note: Replaces the rule against opening a question panel after prose, whose reason was wrong. Text written before any tool call, not only a question panel, reaches the user as another model's short summary, which can change its meaning, so anything they must read goes in the text that ends the turn.

self-carrying-sentences.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. Agents given the old and the new wording acted the same in the same test scenarios.

observable-vs-inferred.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. Agents given the old and the new wording acted the same in the same test scenarios.

second-real-example.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. Agents given the old and the new wording acted the same in the same test scenarios. One clause stayed because the test showed it was needed: an amendment does not inherit the maturity of the rule it extends.

existence-vs-magnitude.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. A check for lost meaning found every instruction kept.

broken-instrument.note: Removed: it rested on a single incident, and the routing rule says one case does not make a rule.

measure-reach.note: Added: a fix scoped to the one example a report names can leave the same cause in place elsewhere, so the rule has the agent check how far the cause reaches first.

prompt-lessons.md.note: Points at the new end-of-turn-text rule in place of the old question-panel rule.

writing-standing-docs.md.note: Rules based on a single incident removed, as the routing rule requires.

writing-executor-briefs.md.note: Rules based on a single incident removed, as the routing rule requires. Three stay even so, because an executor uses them at every checkpoint, where a repeat would cost too much to wait for a second case. All three are about showing that a new test really catches the bug it was written for, rather than passing whatever the code does: if the fix changed how a function is called, undoing it makes the test crash rather than fail, which proves nothing, so put the old behaviour back behind the new call instead; undo only the change being tested, not the whole file, so a failure has one possible cause; and when the test covers code that already worked, so there is no fix to undo, break the code deliberately and check the test fails.

doc-test-probes.md.note: Adds probes for the routing rule's new exception (one checks it works when the user rules a case too costly to wait on, one checks it stays the user's call), and a probe showing whether text written before a tool call still reaches the user only as a summary, with the model and version it was last checked on.

skills/finalise/scripts/context_budget_r.note: Also lists bookkeeping in the files loaded every session: dated notes in brackets, "Provisional" and "cold-tested" tags, and a CLAUDE.md longer than the 200 lines Claude Code's documentation recommends. A dated note on a standing permission is not listed.

skills/finalise/SKILL.md.note: Answers to `/finalize` as well as `/finalise`. Pushes without asking only where a `CLAUDE.md` explicitly pre-authorizes routine pushes; otherwise it still asks.
Step 5 asks for a response to each item the budget report lists as bookkeeping: move it out of the always-loaded file, or say why it stays.

commands/memory-audit.md.note: Part 1 adds a rule-by-rule pass over both CLAUDE.md files: where each rule should load, which sentences are only reasons or bookkeeping and can go, and a check of each trim before it is proposed.

lesson-candidates.md.note: The ledger template gains a field recording a severity ruling, for a rule promoted on one case.
